text:
sanjay: heads up — gpu-serving-3 started spiking with CUDA illegal memory access, containers keep restarting, OOMs on the node :rotating_light:
incident-bot: Incident created INC-2026 · Priority: high · oncall: @oncall
anna: which cluster/node exactly? any customer-facing errors?
sanjay: node gpu-serving-3 (us-east-1a). kube events show repeated OOMKilled and then container restarts. stacktrace shows illegal device address, sometimes aligned-pointer fault.
sanjay: logs:
```
E CUDA: illegal memory access at 0x7fffb3c2 (kernel.cu:124)
W kvcache: missing key for prefix hash
I containerd: killing process pid=2456 `OOMKilled`
```
mike: ok do we need to cordon/drain the node? suggest cordon first, then move critical workloads to gpu-serving-4
lia: can we hot-fallback to the smaller quantized model on that service to avoid GPU allocation? would reduce memory pressure quickly
eric: 3 customer requests failed in the last 5m — CS ticket created, they saw 502s and restarts
oncall: taking this — switching traffic off gpu-serving-3 and starting an emergency rollout to region-west fallback, will also pin replicas to gpu-serving-4
sanjay: suspected kernel race around pagewalks; alignment looks weird in traces, not typical app OOM. capturing kernel oops and will attach
anna: link to live logs? put traces in S3 so we don't lose them after restart
sanjay: uploaded s3://redwood-incident-logs/INC-2026/traces.tgz
anna: thanks. runbook step 4: if illegal deviceaddr, escalate to eng-runtime and consider node reboot after drain
mike: initiating cordon + drain now. command:
```bash
kubectl cordon gpu-serving-3 && kubectl drain gpu-serving-3 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
```
lia: also switching policy for that deployment to smaller batch size and enabling KV prefix cache bypass for that workload to reduce concurrent mem usage
eric: CS notified customers B and C — reduced traffic but they want ETA
oncall: ETA ~30-45m for full stabilization with fallback routing. updating pagerduty and ops status page :hourglass_flowing_sand:
ops-bot: rollout started for service/ml-serving -> image v2.3.1-fallback · started by oncall
sanjay: kernel traces attached show repeated pte walk failures, looks like a sporadic misaligned access from nvcc-compiled kernel, raising with hw/kernel team
mike: if reboots don't stop it we should cordon the whole rack and failover to spare nodes, keep nodes out of the autoscaler until patch applied
lia: tracking note — this might be related to recent allocator change in runtime commit 9f3b12, adding to the incident notes
oncall: handoff to daytime oncall @mike in 10m, will create follow-up doc and postmortem. please add any customer impact summaries here
eric: summary for CS: ~4% request error spike, 3 major customer requests affected (temporary retries resolved for most), no data loss reported
anna: tagging eng-runtime and eng-platform for postmortem. add kernel oops, reproducer script, and timeline to the incident doc
sanjay: temporary mitigation applied: traffic rerouted, node drained, fallback model live. monitoring for recurrence :thumbsup:
ops-bot: incident INC-2026 status -> mitigation in place · watchers: 12
mike: thanks team — next steps: collect reproducer, schedule kernel bisect, runbook review, and customer follow-up.
anna: will open postmortem draft and assign owners. closing Slack thread once we've confirmed stability.
oncall: switching to standby, handing to @mike — keep updates in this thread. :white_check_mark:
